title: Ellington's borrowing and the Ellington Society
summary: They discuss whether Duke took ideas from others; Baron does not care about dirty laundry.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: I’ve heard something about the Ellington Society here, that they’re very, they don’t like to hear anything bad about Duke Ellington. They get like —
You talking about the one in New York City?
Yeah it’s funny. I’m not strict about that myself, but I just think, I don’t even know why it has to come out. Yeah, he probably stole from Billy Strayhorn, you know? Who knows? You know what I mean?
Well didn’t he sort of listen to what people were playing too and take little pieces of what their warm-ups were?

Yeah. Now I don’t know if this actually happened. But check out this possible scenario. (Sorry, Duke.) Where they’re playing “Rose Room” and Johnny Hodges has an idea for a background lick [scats]. I like that. It could have been. I mean the thing is beautiful music came out into the world.
You know, and people got happy. They got elevated. The ones that have to research and find out what the scoundrel aspect of a person is, you know —
Is that going to make you feel better to know that?

Yeah. And some people thrive on this stuff. I mean I don’t like defend it. He was a human being. And was he brilliant, was he a genius, yes. Did he possibly do something a little off-handed? Could be. Do I care? No.
Except when it’s a cool story or something. I just don’t think it’s important, you know. I mean you can find dirty laundry on everybody. You and me even.
